_readme: Fixes applied to the historical-basemaps source when `npm run data` builds the map. years = snapshot years (negative = BCE). n = new name, s = new 'ruled by' (null clears it), note = shown on the map as a data note. Every rule is listed on /about.

rules.name: Thai
rules.note: The source labels most of China in 2000 BCE as 'Thai'. The ancestors of the Tai peoples lived in southern China; the north was home to Longshan-era cultures and the early Erlitou (traditionally Xia) state.
rules.why: An ethnic label stretched over regions it does not describe.

rules.name: Kingdom of Brazil
rules.why: Brazil was an empire from 1822 until the republic was proclaimed in November 1889.

rules.name: Kingdom of Brazil
rules.why: Brazil had been a republic since 1889, independent of Portugal since 1822.

rules.name: White Russia
rules.why: The whole Soviet Union (about 19.5 million km²) was labeled 'White Russia', the old English name for Belarus.

rules.name: Luisiana
rules.why: France ceded Louisiana to Spain in 1762; it went back to France secretly in 1800.

rules.name: Zhoa
rules.why: The Shang dynasty ruled the Yellow River valley c. 1600–1046 BCE; the Zhou came later.

rules.name: Zhoa
rules.why: Misspelling of Zhou (dynasty from 1046 BCE).

rules.name: Hittites
rules.why: The Hittite Empire collapsed around 1180 BCE; small Neo-Hittite kingdoms survived in Syria and Anatolia.

rules.name: Urartu
rules.note: Urartu only emerged around 860 BCE. Earlier, this highland was home to Hurrian peoples (the Mitanni kingdom in 1500 BCE).
rules.why: Urartu appears centuries before it existed.

rules.name: Xiongnu
rules.note: The Xiongnu confederation formed around 209 BCE; in 400 BCE these steppes were held by earlier nomadic peoples.
rules.why: Xiongnu shown about 200 years early.

rules.name: Kushan Empire
rules.why: The Kushan Empire was founded by the Yuezhi around 30 CE.

rules.name: Mauryan Empire
rules.note: The Mauryan Empire fell around 185 BCE. Its successor, the Shunga Empire, was much smaller than the outline shown here.
rules.why: Mauryan Empire shown about 85 years after it fell.

rules.name: Seleucid Kingdom
rules.note: By 100 BCE the Seleucids held little beyond Syria; Parthia had taken Mesopotamia and Iran. The source outline is too large.
rules.why: Outline far larger than Seleucid territory in 100 BCE.

rules.name: Parthian Empire
rules.why: The Sasanians overthrew the Parthians in 224 CE.

rules.name: Persia
rules.why: Persia in 400 CE was the Sasanian Empire.

rules.name: Suren Kingdom
rules.note: The Indo-Parthian (Suren) kingdom had ended by the late 1st century CE; the source keeps it too long.
rules.why: Kingdom shown long after it ended.

rules.name: Satavahanihara
rules.note: The Satavahana dynasty ended around 220 CE; by 300 the Deccan was split among successor states.
rules.why: Dynasty shown after it ended.

rules.name: Jin Empire
rules.why: The Jin dynasty ended in 420; southern China was ruled by the Southern Qi (479–502).

rules.name: Sui Empire
rules.note: Empress Wu Zetian ruled under the name 'Zhou' from 690 to 705, between Tang reigns.
rules.why: The Sui dynasty ended in 618.

rules.name: Sasanian Empire
rules.why: The Sasanian Empire fell to the Arab conquests by 651.

rules.name: Sasanian dependencies
rules.note: The Sasanian Empire had fallen by 651; these lands were ruled by local dynasties or the Caliphate.
rules.why: Shown as Sasanian after the empire fell.

rules.name: Western Gokturk Khaganate
rules.why: The Western Turkic Khaganate fell to the Tang in 657; the Türgesh dominated the region by 699.

rules.name: Koguryo
rules.why: Goguryeo fell in 668; Balhae was founded in its northern lands in 698.

rules.name: Yamato
rules.why: The Yamato period ended in 710.

rules.name: Denmark-Norway
rules.note: Denmark and Norway were not one kingdom in 1000. Denmark's Sweyn Forkbeard controlled much of Norway after the Battle of Svolder (1000); the lasting union dates from 1380. Greenland was a self-governing Norse settlement.
rules.why: Union shown centuries early.

rules.name: Xixia
rules.note: The Western Xia state was proclaimed in 1038; in 1000 this was Tangut territory under Song and Liao influence.
rules.why: Western Xia shown before it was founded.

rules.name: Mongol Empire
rules.why: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan, founding the Mongol Empire, in 1206.

rules.name: Liao
rules.note: The Liao dynasty fell in 1125. In 1200 northern China was ruled by the Jurchen Jin dynasty, which this source does not draw.
rules.why: Liao shown 75 years after it fell; Jin missing.

rules.name: Fatimid Caliphate
rules.why: Saladin ended the Fatimid Caliphate in 1171.

rules.name: Ghaznavid Emirate
rules.why: The Ghurids took the last Ghaznavid lands in 1186.

rules.name: Sultanate of Delhi
rules.why: The Delhi Sultanate was founded in 1206; in 1200 northern India was ruled by the Ghurids.

rules.name: Buwayhid Emirates
rules.note: The Buyid emirates ended in 1062. In 1200 this region was held by Seljuk successor states and the Khwarazmians.
rules.why: Buyids shown long after they ended.

rules.name: Tibet
rules.why: Yuan (Mongol) control of Tibet ended in 1354.

rules.name: Novgorod
rules.why: The Mongol Empire no longer existed as one state in 1400.

rules.name: Inca Empire
rules.why: The last Inca state fell in 1572.

rules.name: Songhai
rules.note: The Songhai Empire fell to Morocco in 1591. This area was then split between the Moroccan Pashalik of Timbuktu and smaller successor states; the source keeps the old outline.
rules.why: Empire shown after its conquest.

rules.name: Vijayanagara
rules.note: The Vijayanagara Empire ended in 1646; its lands passed to Nayak successor states and the Deccan sultanates.
rules.why: Empire shown after it ended.

rules.name: Dutch Brazil
rules.why: The Dutch were expelled from Brazil in 1654.

rules.name: Austrian Empire
rules.why: The Austrian Empire was only proclaimed in 1804.

rules.name: Dutch East Indies
rules.why: Typo in the source ('Neterlands').

rules.name: Quebec
rules.why: France ceded Canada to Britain in 1763.

rules.name: Quebec
rules.why: British since 1763; split into Upper and Lower Canada in 1791.

rules.name: Luisiana
rules.note: Spain secretly agreed to return Louisiana to France in October 1800 (Treaty of San Ildefonso) but governed it until 1803.
rules.why: Spain still governed Louisiana in 1800.

rules.name: Canada
rules.why: Canada was only formed in 1867.

rules.name: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
rules.why: Self-governing since 1810; independence declared in 1816.

rules.name: Manchu Empire
rules.why: The Qing (Manchu) dynasty abdicated in February 1912.

rules.name: Papua New Guinea
rules.why: Papua New Guinea became a country in 1975.

rules.name: Papua New Guinea
rules.why: Papua New Guinea became a country in 1975.

rules.name: Papua New Guinea
rules.why: Papua New Guinea became a country in 1975.

rules.name: Papua New Guinea
rules.n: Territory of Papua and New Guinea
rules.why: Independence came in 1975.

rules.name: USSR
rules.why: The USSR was founded in December 1922.

rules.name: Far Eastern SSR
rules.why: The buffer state's actual name (1920–1922).

rules.name: Far Eastern SSR
rules.why: The Far Eastern Republic joined Soviet Russia in 1922.

rules.name: Iran
rules.why: The country asked to be called Iran internationally in 1935.

rules.name: Zaire (Belgium)
rules.why: The name Zaire was used only from 1971 to 1997.

rules.name: Zaire
rules.why: The name Zaire was used only from 1971 to 1997.

rules.name: Zaire
rules.why: Independent as the Republic of the Congo in June 1960; Zaire only from 1971.

rules.name: Zaire
rules.why: Renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 1997.

rules.name: Tanzania, United Republic of
rules.why: Tanzania was formed in 1964; this was the British mandate of Tanganyika.

rules.name: Tanzania, United Republic of
rules.why: Tanganyika became independent in December 1961.

rules.name: Tanzania, United Republic of
rules.why: Shorter common name.

rules.name: Zambia
rules.why: Zambia became independent in 1964.

rules.name: Zimbabwe
rules.why: Zimbabwe became independent in 1980.

rules.name: Rhodesia
rules.why: Official name of the colony.

rules.name: Botswana
rules.why: Botswana became independent in 1966.

rules.name: Malaysia
rules.why: Malaysia was formed in 1963.

rules.name: Malaysia
rules.why: Malaysia was formed in 1963.

rules.name: Hejaz
rules.why: Ibn Saud conquered the Hejaz in 1925.

rules.name: Hejaz
rules.why: Part of Saudi Arabia since 1932.

rules.name: Chinese Warlords
rules.why: The Nationalist government reunified most of China in 1928.

rules.name: Chinese warlords
rules.note: Japan occupied much of eastern China from 1937, which this snapshot does not show.
rules.why: The Nationalist government ruled China in 1938.

rules.name: India
rules.why: India and Pakistan became independent in August 1947.

rules.name: Pakistan
rules.why: Pakistan was created in August 1947.

rules.name: Namibia
rules.why: Namibia became independent in 1990.

rules.name: Central African Republic
rules.why: Independent as the Central African Republic in 1960.

rules.name: Burkina Faso
rules.note: France dissolved Upper Volta among neighbouring colonies from 1932 to 1947.
rules.why: Renamed Burkina Faso in 1984.

rules.name: Burkina Faso
rules.why: Renamed Burkina Faso in 1984.

rules.name: Mali
rules.why: Mali became independent in 1960.

rules.name: Western Sahara
rules.why: Spain held the territory until 1975–76.

rules.name: Tibet
rules.note: Under the control of the People's Republic of China since 1950–51.
rules.why: Shown as independent in 1960.

rules.name: Vietnam
rules.note: Divided into North and South Vietnam from 1954 to 1976.
rules.why: Shown as one country in 1960.

geometry.what: Split the 'Great Khanate' into the Ming Empire (outline from the 1492 snapshot) and the Northern Yuan.
geometry.why: The Ming dynasty had ruled China since 1368; the source still drew the Mongol Yuan state.

geometry.what: Separated Svalbard from Norway / Denmark-Norway / Sweden–Norway.
geometry.why: Svalbard belonged to no country until the 1920 Svalbard Treaty, which took effect in 1925.

geometry.what: Named Switzerland, which the source draws without a name (it showed as 'not mapped'). The outline is the source's own.
geometry.why: Switzerland has been an independent country throughout; the source's 1994, 2000 and 2010 snapshots leave its name blank.

geometry.what: Joined Gotland to Sweden and Lewis and Harris to the United Kingdom, which the source draws without a name. In 1994 the source draws Taiwan twice; the map uses its unnamed outline (the one 2000 and 2010 use) instead of the older named one.
geometry.why: They belonged to those countries throughout; without a name they showed as 'not mapped' (around Taiwan, as a blank rim).

geometry.what: Named Tasmania, which the source draws without a name, as the British colony it was, like the mainland colonies: Van Diemen's Land in 1815, 'Tasmania (UK)' in 1878–1900.
geometry.why: Tasmania was a British colony from 1803 until federation in 1901 (Van Diemen's Land until 1856); without a name it showed as 'not mapped'.

geometry.what: Separated Crimea from Russia as its own disputed shape.
geometry.why: Russia has controlled Crimea since 2014, but most UN members recognize it as part of Ukraine.

geometry.what: Gave the blank strips along coasts to the shapes beside them: thin strips (up to about 20 km wide) everywhere, and every strip along Australia's coast. A strip that borders several shapes is shared out, each part going to the nearest. In 1600–1815 the thin coastal slivers of the older 'Australian aboriginal hunter-gatherers' shape go to the nations beside them the same way.
geometry.why: The source's outlines often stop short of the real coastline, so strips of land showed as 'not mapped' between its shapes and the sea (in Australia from 1600, also as slivers of the older shape the source still draws underneath the nations).

geometry.what: Gave thin unnamed slivers wedged between two or more neighbours (up to about 30 km wide, with no coast) to the neighbour each shares most border with. For example, a 29,000 km² wedge south of Great Slave Lake in 900.
geometry.why: Where the source's outlines of neighbours don't quite meet, the gap between them showed as 'not mapped'. Wider unclaimed areas stay as the source draws them.

geometry.what: Filled land the source leaves blank (for example Sumbawa in Indonesia) as 'not mapped in the source', so the map has no false sea.
geometry.why: Islands and coasts missing from the historical outlines.
